  *****NOTE FROM THE CITY*****

Doors to the City Council Chamber will open at 1:30 p.m. for Open Session. Please be mindful that
seating is limited and available on a first come, first served basis.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting
convenience:

  ¡  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.
  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video,
  at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
 comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities A
1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any
person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe
and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contact
the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280,  FAX at 310 -412-5533, One Manchester
Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email
to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled
meeting.

Inglewood, California
  November 21, 2023

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  November 21, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
  of 2:01 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members/ Joint Powers
  Authority Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member Gray.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item
  on the Agendas.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  November 17, 2023, in the amount of $6,691,289.67, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Gray.

301  PARTIAL PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – WILLDAN ENGINEERING, INC. Staff
  report dated November 21, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members authorize a partial payment of an invoice submitted by Willdan Engineering, Inc.
  (Willdan), dated August 25, 2023, in the amount of $4,310 (which exceeds the City Council
  approved contract amount of $250,000 for Fiscal Year 2022-2023), for augmented code
  enforcement services at SoFi Stadium on August 19, 2023 (Rams vs. Raiders).

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby authorize partial payment. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.
 November 21, 2023

142  AGREEMENT NO. 22-125 TERMINATED – MGT CONSULTING GROUP, INC.
  Staff report dated November 21, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and
  Council Members terminate the Agreement (Agreement No. 22-125) with MGT Consulting
  Group, Inc.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby terminate Agreement No. 22-125. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

160  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-052 APPROVED – POLAR
  BEAR LIGHTING, INC. Staff report dated November 21, 2023, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members award a contract and approve a three
  (3)-year agreement (with the option to extend for two additional years in one-year
  increments) with Polar Bear Lighting, Inc., for Christmas Tree and Tree Lighting
  Decoration Services, per RFP-0211.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement No. 24-052 in the
  total amount of $116,100 ($38,700 annually). The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

160  PAYMENT OF INVOICE AUTHORIZED – ERENDIRA BERNAL. Staff report dated
  November 21, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members
  authorize payment of an invoice submitted by Erendira Bernal for providing interactive and
  educational workshops for the City’s Dia de Los Muertos Celebration on Saturday, October
  28, 2023.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby authorize the payment in the amount of $3,000. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

160  PAYMENT OF INVOICE AUTHORIZED – UNITED SITE SERVICES. Staff report
  dated November 21, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members authorize payment of an invoice submitted by United Site Services, for the rental
  of a portable restroom and handwashing sink.

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $310.90. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

103.3  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-053 APPROVED – HHJ
  CONSTRUCTION, INC.; CITY CONTROLLED AND CONTINGENCY
  APPROVED; RESOLUTION NO. 24-15 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2023-2024 BUDGET. Staff report dated November 21, 2023, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members award a contract and approve an
  Agreement with HHJ Construction, Inc. (HHJ) to provide residential sound insulation work
  on 74 residential units (RSI Phase XV, Group 38).

  2
 November 21, 2023

  It was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Award contract and approve Agreement No. 24-053 in an
  amount not to exceed $1,570,000; 2) Approve a City controlled and directed 10%
  contingency of $157,000, and special expense of $25,826 per Bid No. CB-23-21; and 3)
  Adopt Resolution No. 24-15 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2023/2024 ANNUAL BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

142  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-054 APPROVED – V.T.P.
  INC. Staff report dated November 21, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor
  and Council Members award a contract and approve a three-year agreement (with the option
  to extend two additional years in one-year increments) with V.T.P. Inc. for the Installation,
  Removal, and Repair of Various Facility Flooring, per RFB-0165 Re-Issue.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement No. 24-054 in the
  annual amount of $224,394.33. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

142  STIPEND AGREEMENT NOS. 23-205 AMENDED – INGLEWOOD TRANSIT
  CONNECTOR (ITC) PROJECT; RESOLUTION NO. 24-16 ADOPTED -
  AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 BUDGET. Staff report dated November
  21, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members amend the
  Stipend Agreements for the Inglewood Transit Connector (ITC) Project to authorize
  payment of up to $3,500,000 to each eligible proposer.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that the City Council
  does hereby: 1) Amend the Stipend Agreement Nos. 23-205; and 2) Adopt Resolution No.
  24-16 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 24-055 APPROVED – SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA GAS
  COMPANY (SOCALGAS); MAYOR AUTHORIZED – EXECUTION OF
  AGREEMENT NO. 24-055. Staff report dated November 21, 2023, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve a Facilities Relocation
  Agreement (Agreement) with Southern California Gas Company (SoCalGas) for the ITC
  Project.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 24-055; and 2) Authorize the
  Mayor to execute Agreement No. 24-055. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

  3
 November 21, 2023

301  PUBLIC HEARING SET – ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 23-00006 (ZCA23-
  00006). Staff report dated November 21, 2023, was presented requesting that the Mayor
  and Council Members set a public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment No. 23-
  00006 (ZCA23-00006), establishing regulations for Accessory Dwelling Units in Chapter
  12 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, Citywide. \

  Mayor Butts set the public hearing for December 5, 2023, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson thanked the Delta Kappa
  Chapter for allowing her to attend their November 18, 2023, chapter meeting. Her
  experience with the Delta Kappa Chapter was pleasant, and she enjoyed spending time
  with them. She also stated that the ladies are enthused about getting involved and active with
  what the City of Inglewood is doing. The City Clerk also reported about her  attendance at
  Cinder Eller’s Glass Slipper Event, which was well attended and blessed many children. She
  mentioned the privilege of taking a picture with Miss Universe, and  it was amazing
  to stand alongside her. Additionally, she added that she was privileged to participate in the
  event and thanked Cinder Eller for all she does in the  community  and  Miss
  Universe for stopping by and encouraging young people.

  Furthermore, the City Clerk reported that she and her staff attended the Holiday Turkey
  Giveaway. She thanked her staff for helping out: Thomas Uwal, Acting Parks and
  Recreation Director; Teresa Estrada, Parks and Recreation Superintendent; Hollywood
  Park Staff; SoFi Stadium; the sponsors; City of Inglewood Staff; and the volunteers.
  Finally, she mentioned that this was her first Thanksgiving without her parents and wished
  everyone a Happy Thanksgiving.

127  COUNCIL INITIATIVE

  Mayor Butts:

  PURCHASE OF GIFT CARDS APPROVED – DISTRIBUTION TO
  DISADVANTAGED INGLEWOOD UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT (IUSD)
  STUDENTS AND THEIR FAMILIES FOR CHRISTMAS 2023. Initiative by Mayor
  James T. Butts, Jr., dated November 21, 2023, was presented recommending that City
  Council approve the purchase of gift cards, in an amount not to exceed $95,000, for
  distribution to disadvantaged Inglewood Unified School District (IUSD) students and their
  families for Christmas 2023.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve purchase of gift cards for distribution to
  disadvantaged Inglewood Unified School District (IUSD) Students and their families for
  Christmas 2023. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

127.2  COUNCIL INITIATIVE

  Council Member Faulk:

  CITY SPONSORSHIP APPROVED – 2023 DISTRICT 4 HOLIDAY DONATION
  DRIVE. Initiative by Council Member Faulk recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members approve City Sponsorship of the 2023 District 4 Holiday Donation Drive to be
  held on Sunday, December 3, 2023, at Darby Dixon Park, and Friday, December 8, 2023,

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve the City Sponsorship of the 2023 District 4 Holiday

  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.
